```{ojs}
// The test toggle. A stock radio (the same control the PPV page uses for
// its Shuffled/Sorted switch) rather than a bespoke widget, so it wears the

  for (const id of ["t", "F", "chi"]) options.set(testMeta[id].label, id)
  return Inputs.radio(options, {label: "Test", value})
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// One flat map of every field across all three tests -- the keys are
// disjoint (t/F use the group fields, chi uses observed/expected), so
// applyExampleParams only ever touches the keys an example actually sets.
exampleFieldSelectors = ({
  mean1: '[data-example-field="mean1"]',
  sd1: '[data-example-field="sd1"]',
  n1: '[data-example-field="n1"]',
  mean2: '[data-example-field="mean2"]',
  sd2: '[data-example-field="sd2"]',
  n2: '[data-example-field="n2"]',
  observed: '[data-example-field="observed"]',
  expected: '[data-example-field="expected"]'
})
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// A one-time native "change" listener on the rebuilt <select> (not an OJS
// cell reactive on exampleSelect's value -- a <select> fires both "input"
// and "change" per pick, which would run a reactive cell twice and race).
// This cell re-runs when viewof exampleSelect is rebuilt on a test switch,
// re-attaching to the fresh node.
applyExampleFromSelect = {
  const nativeSelect = (viewof exampleSelect).querySelector("select")
  if (!nativeSelect) return
  nativeSelect.addEventListener("change", () => {
    const example = (viewof exampleSelect).value
    if (!example) return
    VM.ui.applyExampleParams(exampleFieldSelectors, example.params, viewof runTrigger)
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
// Run test commits the data fields above -- edits don't take effect (and
// don't recompute result/plots on every keystroke) until this is clicked.
// The alpha slider and the alternative-hypothesis control below stay live.
viewof runTrigger = {
  const button = Inputs.button("Run test", {value: 0, reduce: v => v + 1})
  button.classList.add("ojs-auto", "ojs-end")
  return button
}
```

```{ojs}
// Always-live: switches which tail(s) count toward the p-value. Its own
// group below the commit button, like every other always-live panel
// control on the site. Hidden for the chi-square test, which is
// inherently one-sided (right tail).
viewof tail = {
  activeTest
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  const value = ["two-sided", "greater", "less"].includes(params.get("tail")) ? params.get("tail") : "two-sided"
  const labels = activeTest === "F"
    ? {
        "two-sided": "Two-sided — the spreads just differ",
        "greater": "One-sided — Group 1 is more variable",
        "less": "One-sided — Group 1 is less variable"
      }
    : {
        "two-sided": "Two-sided — the means just differ",
        "greater": "One-sided — Group 1's mean is higher",
        "less": "One-sided — Group 1's mean is lower"
      }
  return Inputs.select(["two-sided", "greater", "less"], {label: "What counts as a difference?", value, format: key => labels[key]})
}
```

<div class="htest-explain">Leave this on <strong>two-sided</strong> unless you committed to a direction <em>before</em> seeing the data. A one-sided test puts all of the false-alarm risk in one tail, so it flags a difference in that direction sooner — and is blind to one going the other way.</div>

```{ojs}
// Shows the field group that matches the active test and hides the other,
// and hides the tail control for chi-square. The groups all stay in the
// DOM either way, so document.querySelector (data-example-field) still
// finds every field regardless of which test is showing.
applyTestVisibility = {

  const tf = document.getElementById("htest-group-tf")
  const chi = document.getElementById("htest-group-chi")
  const tailField = document.getElementById("htest-tail-field")

  if (chi) chi.style.display = test === "chi" ? "" : "none"

}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// committed snapshots the data fields when Run test fires (it reads the
// stable `viewof` DOM nodes, not the reactive values, so it doesn't rerun
// on keystrokes) and writes every field back into the URL so the address
// bar is a shareable link. It still runs once on load, so the first render
// uses the URL/default values with no click.
committed = {
  runTrigger
  const math = window.math
  const num = text => VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, text)

  const raw = {
    mean1: (viewof mean1).value, sd1: (viewof sd1).value, n1: (viewof n1).value,
    mean2: (viewof mean2).value, sd2: (viewof sd2).value, n2: (viewof n2).value,
    observed: (viewof observed).value, expected: (viewof expected).value
  }

  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  for (const key of Object.keys(raw)) params.set(key, raw[key])
  history.replaceState(null, "", `${window.location.pathname}?${params}`)

  return {
    mean1: num(raw.mean1), sd1: num(raw.sd1), n1: num(raw.n1),
    mean2: num(raw.mean2), sd2: num(raw.sd2), n2: num(raw.n2),
    observedText: raw.observed, expectedText: raw.expected,
    seedKey: [raw.mean1, raw.sd1, raw.n1, raw.mean2, raw.sd2, raw.n2].join("|")
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
```
```{ojs}
// Inverts a monotone CDF by bisection -- used for the critical value(s)
// drawn on the distribution. `lo`/`hi` bracket the root; 120 halvings take
// the interval far below double precision.
quantile = function (cdf, p, lo, hi) {
  let a = lo
  let b = hi
  for (let i = 0; i < 120; i++) {
    const mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
    if (cdf(mid) < p) a = mid
    else b = mid
  }
  return 0.5 * (a + b)
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// result: turns the committed inputs into a test statistic, its null
// distribution, a p-value, the critical value(s) at the current alpha, and
// a reject / fail-to-reject decision. Returns { ok: false } on unusable
// input, which the plots render as an empty state.
result = {
  const test = activeTest
  const alphaVal = alpha
  const c = committed

  if (test === "t" || test === "F") {
    const {mean1, sd1, n1, mean2, sd2, n2} = c
    let finite = true
    for (const v of [mean1, sd1, n1, mean2, sd2, n2]) {
      if (!Number.isFinite(v)) finite = false
    }
    if (!finite || sd1 <= 0 || sd2 <= 0 || n1 < 2 || n2 < 2) return {ok: false, test}

    if (test === "t") {
      const df = n1 + n2 - 2
      const pooledVar = ((n1 - 1) * sd1 * sd1 + (n2 - 1) * sd2 * sd2) / df
      const se = Math.sqrt(pooledVar * (1 / n1 + 1 / n2))
      const statistic = (mean1 - mean2) / se
      const cdf = x => VM.distributions.studentTCdf(x, df)
      const pdf = x => VM.distributions.studentTPdf(x, df)
      const Q = p => quantile(cdf, p, -1e4, 1e4)

      let pValue, critLines, pValueTails, critAbs
      if (tail === "two-sided") {
        pValue = 2 * (1 - cdf(Math.abs(statistic)))
        critAbs = Q(1 - alphaVal / 2)
        critLines = [-critAbs, critAbs]
        pValueTails = [{from: -Infinity, to: -Math.abs(statistic)}, {from: Math.abs(statistic), to: Infinity}]
      } else if (tail === "greater") {
        pValue = 1 - cdf(statistic)
        critAbs = Q(1 - alphaVal)
        critLines = [critAbs]
        pValueTails = [{from: statistic, to: Infinity}]
      } else {
        pValue = cdf(statistic)
        critAbs = Q(1 - alphaVal)
        critLines = [-critAbs]
        pValueTails = [{from: -Infinity, to: statistic}]
      }

      return {
        ok: true, test, df, statistic, pdf, cdf,
        pValue, critLines, pValueTails, critAbs, se, pooledVar,
        reject: pValue < alphaVal,
        mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2, n1, n2
      }
    }

    // F-test: ratio of the two sample variances.
    const df1 = n1 - 1
    const df2 = n2 - 1
    const statistic = (sd1 * sd1) / (sd2 * sd2)
    const cdf = x => VM.distributions.fCdf(x, df1, df2)
    const pdf = x => VM.distributions.fPdf(x, df1, df2)
    const Q = p => quantile(cdf, p, 0, 1e7)
    const cprob = cdf(statistic)

    let pValue, critLines, pValueTails
    if (tail === "two-sided") {
      const minTail = Math.min(cprob, 1 - cprob)
      pValue = 2 * minTail
      critLines = [Q(alphaVal / 2), Q(1 - alphaVal / 2)]
      pValueTails = [{from: -Infinity, to: Q(minTail)}, {from: Q(1 - minTail), to: Infinity}]
    } else if (tail === "greater") {
      pValue = 1 - cprob
      critLines = [Q(1 - alphaVal)]
      pValueTails = [{from: statistic, to: Infinity}]
    } else {
      pValue = cprob
      critLines = [Q(alphaVal)]
      pValueTails = [{from: -Infinity, to: statistic}]
    }

    return {
      ok: true, test, df1, df2, statistic, pdf, cdf,
      pValue, critLines, pValueTails,
      reject: pValue < alphaVal,
      mean1, mean2, sd1, sd2, n1, n2
    }
  }

  // Chi-square goodness-of-fit.
  const math = window.math
  const parseList = text => {
    const out = []
    for (const token of String(text).split(/[,\s]+/)) {
      if (token === "") continue
      const value = VM.expressions.makeNumber(math, token)
      out.push(value)
    }
    return out
  }

  const obs = parseList(c.observedText)
  let obsValid = obs.length >= 2
  for (const v of obs) {
    if (!Number.isFinite(v) || v < 0) obsValid = false
  }
  if (!obsValid) return {ok: false, test}

  let total = 0
  for (const v of obs) total += v

  const expText = String(c.expectedText).trim().toLowerCase()
  const exp = []
  if (expText === "" || expText === "uniform") {
    for (let i = 0; i < obs.length; i++) exp.push(total / obs.length)
  } else {
    const list = parseList(c.expectedText)
    let listValid = list.length === obs.length
    let listSum = 0
    for (const v of list) {
      if (!Number.isFinite(v) || v <= 0) listValid = false
      listSum += v
    }
    if (!listValid) return {ok: false, test}
    // A list that sums to 1 is read as probabilities; otherwise as raw
    // expected counts.
    const asProbabilities = Math.abs(listSum - 1) < 1e-6
    for (const v of list) exp.push(asProbabilities ? v * total : v)
  }

  const df = obs.length - 1
  const categories = []
  let statistic = 0
  for (let i = 0; i < obs.length; i++) {
    const contrib = (obs[i] - exp[i]) * (obs[i] - exp[i]) / exp[i]
    statistic += contrib
    categories.push({label: `${i + 1}`, o: obs[i], e: exp[i], contrib})
  }
  const cdf = x => VM.distributions.chiSquaredCdf(x, df)
  const pdf = x => VM.distributions.chiSquaredPdf(x, df)
  const critValue = quantile(cdf, 1 - alphaVal, 0, 1e7)
  const pValue = 1 - cdf(statistic)

  return {
    ok: true, test, df, statistic, pdf, cdf, categories, total,
    pValue, critLines: [critValue], pValueTails: [{from: statistic, to: Infinity}],
    reject: pValue < alphaVal
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// setup: samples the active null distribution and turns result's abstract
// tail intervals into polygons the chart can fill.
setup = {
  const r = result
  if (!r.ok) return {ok: false, test: r.test}
  const test = r.test

  let lo, hi
  let crit = 0
  for (const value of r.critLines) crit = Math.max(crit, Math.abs(value))
  if (test === "t") {
    const reach = Math.max(4, Math.abs(r.statistic) * 1.15, crit * 1.25)
    lo = -reach
    hi = reach
  } else {
    lo = 0
    const base = test === "chi" ? r.df * 2.2 + 6 : 4
    hi = Math.max(r.statistic * 1.4, crit * 1.3, base, 5)
  }

  const N = 420
  const xs = []
  const ys = []
  const eps = test === "t" ? 0 : (hi - lo) / N * 0.5
  for (let i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    let x
    if (test === "t") x = lo + (hi - lo) * i / (N - 1)
    else x = eps + (hi - eps) * i / (N - 1)
    xs.push(x)
    ys.push(r.pdf(x))
  }

  // y-axis max: skip the first few samples so an F/chi density that blows
  // up near 0 (df1 = 1, or df < 2) doesn't set the whole scale.
  let ymax = 0
  const startAt = test === "t" ? 0 : Math.round(N * 0.04)
  for (let i = startAt; i < ys.length; i++) {
    if (Number.isFinite(ys[i]) && ys[i] > ymax) ymax = ys[i]
  }
  if (!(ymax > 0)) ymax = 1

  const clampX = x => Math.max(lo, Math.min(hi, x))
  const shades = []
  for (const region of r.pValueTails) {
    const from = clampX(region.from === -Infinity ? lo : region.from)
    const to = clampX(region.to === Infinity ? hi : region.to)
    if (!(to > from)) continue
    const seg = {x: [], y: []}
    const steps = 100
    for (let i = 0; i <= steps; i++) {
      const x = from + (to - from) * i / steps
      let px = x
      if (test !== "t" && px <= 0) px = 1e-9
      seg.x.push(x)
      seg.y.push(r.pdf(px))
    }
    shades.push(seg)
  }

  return {ok: true, test, xs, ys, ymax, lo, hi, shades, statLine: r.statistic, critLines: r.critLines}
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// dataPlot: the "what the data looks like" panel above the distribution.
// For t / F it draws each group as a strip of jittered points (seeded from
// the committed stats, so stable across re-renders) with its mean and
// +/- 1 and 2 SD whiskers; the t view adds an observed-difference vs.
// significance-threshold comparison, the F view shades each group's +/- 1
// SD band so the width ratio is the F ratio. For chi-square it draws
// observed vs. expected counts as grouped bars, labelled with each
// category's contribution to the statistic.
dataPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  const hashString = s => {
    let h = 2166136261
    for (let i = 0; i < s.length; i++) {
      h ^= s.charCodeAt(i)
      h = Math.imul(h, 16777619)
    }
    return h >>> 0
  }

  return (r, c, colors) => {
    const data = []
    const shapes = []
    const annotations = []
    let layout

    if (!r.ok) {
      layout = VM.plotting.layout({
        xaxis: {visible: false},
        yaxis: {visible: false},
        annotations: VM.plotting.emptyState("Check the inputs above — every field needs a number, sizes ≥ 2, SDs > 0.")
      })
    } else if (r.test === "chi") {
      const xs = []
      const obs = []
      const exp = []
      const contribText = []
      for (const cat of r.categories) {
        xs.push(cat.label)
        obs.push(cat.o)
        exp.push(cat.e)
        contribText.push(cat.contrib.toFixed(2))
      }
      data.push({
        x: xs, y: exp, type: "bar", name: "Expected", showlegend: false,
        marker: {color: VM.plotting.alpha("muted", 0.45), line: {color: colors.muted, width: 1}},
        hovertemplate: "category %{x}<br>expected %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>"
      })
      data.push({
        x: xs, y: obs, type: "bar", name: "Observed", showlegend: false,
        marker: {color: colors.fn},
        text: contribText, textposition: "outside",
        hovertemplate: "category %{x}<br>observed %{y}<extra></extra>"
      })
      annotations.push({
        x: 0.5, xref: "paper", y: 1.06, yref: "paper", xanchor: "center", showarrow: false,
        text: `each bar label is that category's (O−E)²/E — they sum to χ² = ${r.statistic.toFixed(2)}`,
        font: {size: 11, color: colors.ink}
      })
      layout = VM.plotting.layout({
        barmode: "group",
        xaxis: {title: "category", type: "category"},
        yaxis: {title: "count", rangemode: "tozero"},
        showlegend: false,
        margin: {t: 44},
        annotations
      })
    } else {
      const groups = [
        {mean: c.mean1, sd: c.sd1, n: c.n1, y: 1, token: "ok", color: colors.ok, name: "Group 1"},
        {mean: c.mean2, sd: c.sd2, n: c.n2, y: 0, token: "alt", color: colors.alt, name: "Group 2"}
      ]
      const rng = VM.sampling.seededRandom(hashString(c.seedKey))
      const gauss = VM.sampling.gaussianRandom(rng)
      const allX = []

      for (const g of groups) {
        const k = Math.max(6, Math.min(60, Math.round(g.n)))
        const px = []
        const py = []
        for (let i = 0; i < k; i++) {
          const xv = g.mean + g.sd * gauss()
          px.push(xv)
          py.push(g.y + (rng() - 0.5) * 0.34)
          allX.push(xv)
        }
        allX.push(g.mean - 2.5 * g.sd, g.mean + 2.5 * g.sd)

        if (r.test === "F") {
          shapes.push({
            type: "rect", xref: "x", yref: "y",
            x0: g.mean - g.sd, x1: g.mean + g.sd, y0: g.y - 0.24, y1: g.y + 0.24,
            fillcolor: VM.plotting.alpha(g.token, 0.16), line: {width: 0}, layer: "below"
          })
        }
        shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "y", x0: g.mean - 2 * g.sd, x1: g.mean + 2 * g.sd, y0: g.y, y1: g.y, line: {color: colors.muted, width: 1.5}})
        shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "y", x0: g.mean - g.sd, x1: g.mean + g.sd, y0: g.y, y1: g.y, line: {color: g.color, width: 4}})

        data.push({
          x: px, y: py, type: "scatter", mode: "markers", name: g.name, showlegend: false,
          marker: {color: VM.plotting.alpha(g.token, 0.5), size: 7, line: {color: g.color, width: 0.5}},
          hovertemplate: `${g.name}<br>value ≈ %{x:.3g}<extra></extra>`
        })
        data.push({
          x: [g.mean], y: [g.y], type: "scatter", mode: "markers", showlegend: false,
          marker: {color: g.color, size: 15, symbol: "diamond", line: {color: colors.halo, width: 1.5}},
          hovertemplate: `${g.name} mean = %{x:.4g}<extra></extra>`
        })
      }

      if (r.test === "t") {
        const dObs = Math.abs(c.mean1 - c.mean2)
        const threshold = r.critAbs * r.se
        const x0 = Math.min(c.mean1, c.mean2)
        allX.push(x0 + dObs, x0 + threshold)
        shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "y", x0, x1: x0 + threshold, y0: 1.78, y1: 1.78, line: {color: colors.accent2, width: 3, dash: "dot"}})
        shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "y", x0, x1: x0 + dObs, y0: 1.55, y1: 1.55, line: {color: r.reject ? colors.warn : colors.muted, width: 7}})
        annotations.push({x: x0 + dObs, y: 1.55, yref: "y", xanchor: "left", showarrow: false, text: `  your gap = ${dObs.toFixed(2)}`, font: {size: 11, color: colors.ink}})
        annotations.push({x: x0 + threshold, y: 1.78, yref: "y", xanchor: "left", showarrow: false, text: `  gap needed to be significant = ${threshold.toFixed(2)}`, font: {size: 11, color: colors.ink}})
      } else {
        annotations.push({
          x: 0.5, xref: "paper", y: 1.9, yref: "y", xanchor: "center", showarrow: false,
          text: `s₁ = ${c.sd1.toFixed(2)},  s₂ = ${c.sd2.toFixed(2)}   →   F = s₁² / s₂² = ${r.statistic.toFixed(3)}`,
          font: {size: 11, color: colors.ink}
        })
      }

      const xRange = VM.plotting.paddedRange(allX, {relativePadding: 0.08, minPadding: 1})
      layout = VM.plotting.layout({
        xaxis: {title: "value", range: [xRange.lo, xRange.hi], zeroline: false},
        yaxis: {range: [-0.7, r.test === "t" ? 2.1 : 2.05], tickvals: [0, 1], ticktext: ["Group 2", "Group 1"], zeroline: false},
        shapes,
        annotations,
        showlegend: false,
        hovermode: "closest"
      })
    }

    const config = VM.plotting.config()
    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "htest-data-box"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, config)
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| output: false
// mainPlot: the null sampling distribution, with the observed statistic
// marked, the critical value(s) at the current alpha dashed in, and the
// p-value tail(s) shaded.
mainPlot = {
  const Plotly = window.Plotly
  let _plotDiv = null

  return (s, r, colors) => {
    const data = []
    const shapes = []
    const annotations = []
    const sym = s.ok ? testMeta[r.test].symbol : ""

    if (!s.ok) {
      const layout = VM.plotting.layout({
        xaxis: {visible: false},
        yaxis: {visible: false},
        annotations: VM.plotting.emptyState("No result to show yet.")
      })
      if (!_plotDiv) {
        _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
        _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
        Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, [], layout, VM.plotting.config())
        VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
      } else {
        Plotly.react(_plotDiv, [], layout, VM.plotting.config())
      }
      return _plotDiv
    }

    // When the statistic sits at the centre of the distribution (p ≈ 1),
    // "as extreme or more" is essentially the whole curve -- shading all of
    // it just reads as a bug, so show a note instead.
    if (r.pValue > 0.99) {
      annotations.push({
        x: 0.5, xref: "paper", y: 0.55, yref: "paper", xanchor: "center", showarrow: false,
        text: "your statistic sits in the middle of the distribution —<br>almost every value is \"as extreme or more\", so p ≈ 1",
        font: {size: 11, color: colors.ink}
      })
    } else {
      for (const seg of s.shades) {
        data.push({
          x: seg.x, y: seg.y, type: "scatter", mode: "none", fill: "tozeroy",
          fillcolor: VM.plotting.alpha("warn", 0.4), showlegend: false, hoverinfo: "skip"
        })
      }
    }
    data.push({
      x: s.xs, y: s.ys, type: "scatter", mode: "lines", name: "null distribution", showlegend: false,
      line: {color: colors.fn, width: 2.5},
      hovertemplate: `${sym} = %{x:.3g}<br>density %{y:.3g}<extra></extra>`
    })

    for (const cx of s.critLines) {
      if (cx < s.lo || cx > s.hi) continue
      shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "paper", x0: cx, x1: cx, y0: 0, y1: 1, line: {color: colors.accent2, width: 1.5, dash: "dash"}})
    }
    annotations.push({
      x: s.critLines.length && s.critLines[s.critLines.length - 1] <= s.hi ? s.critLines[s.critLines.length - 1] : s.hi,
      y: 1, yref: "paper", yanchor: "bottom", xanchor: "center", showarrow: false,
      text: `critical value${s.critLines.length > 1 ? "s" : ""} at α = ${alpha}`,
      font: {size: 10, color: colors.accent2}
    })

    if (s.statLine >= s.lo && s.statLine <= s.hi) {
      shapes.push({type: "line", xref: "x", yref: "paper", x0: s.statLine, x1: s.statLine, y0: 0, y1: 1, line: {color: colors.ink, width: 2}})
      annotations.push({
        x: s.statLine, y: 0.5, yref: "paper", yanchor: "bottom", xanchor: "left", showarrow: false,
        text: `  ${sym} = ${r.statistic.toFixed(3)}`,
        font: {size: 12, color: colors.ink}
      })
    }

    const pText = r.pValue < 1e-4 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${r.pValue.toFixed(4)}`
    annotations.push({
      x: 0.98, xref: "paper", y: 0.96, yref: "paper", xanchor: "right", yanchor: "top", showarrow: false,
      text: `${pText}  ·  ${r.reject ? "significant" : "not significant"} at α = ${alpha}`,
      font: {size: 13, color: r.reject ? colors.warn : colors.ink},
      bgcolor: VM.plotting.alpha(r.reject ? "warn" : "muted", 0.12),
      borderpad: 4
    })

    const layout = VM.plotting.layout({
      xaxis: {title: `${sym} statistic`, range: [s.lo, s.hi], zeroline: r.test === "t"},
      yaxis: {title: "density", range: [0, s.ymax * 1.18], rangemode: "tozero"},
      shapes,
      annotations,
      hovermode: "closest",
      uirevision: "static"
    })

    if (!_plotDiv) {
      _plotDiv = document.createElement("div")
      _plotDiv.className = "plotly-box-large"
      Plotly.newPlot(_plotDiv, data, layout, VM.plotting.config())
      VM.plotting.autoResize(_plotDiv)
    } else {
      Plotly.react(_plotDiv, data, layout, VM.plotting.config())
    }
    return _plotDiv
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
bridge = {
  const r = result
  if (!r.ok) return md``
  if (r.test === "t") {
    return md`<div class="htest-bridge">Boil the two groups down to <strong>one number</strong>: divide the gap between the means by its standard error.<br>
<code>t = (${r.mean1.toFixed(2)} − ${r.mean2.toFixed(2)}) / ${r.se.toFixed(3)} = ${r.statistic.toFixed(3)}</code><br>
The gap is <strong>${Math.abs(r.statistic).toFixed(2)} standard errors</strong> wide. Now see how often plain noise produces a <em>t</em> that far from 0:</div>`
  }
  if (r.test === "F") {
    return md`<div class="htest-bridge">Boil the two groups down to <strong>one number</strong>: the ratio of their variances.<br>
<code>F = ${(r.sd1 * r.sd1).toFixed(2)} / ${(r.sd2 * r.sd2).toFixed(2)} = ${r.statistic.toFixed(3)}</code><br>
Equal spreads would put this near 1. Now see how often noise alone pushes it this far:</div>`
  }
  const parts = []
  for (const cat of r.categories) parts.push(cat.contrib.toFixed(2))
  return md`<div class="htest-bridge">Boil the whole table down to <strong>one number</strong>: add up every category's (O−E)²/E.<br>
<code>χ² = ${parts.join(" + ")} = ${r.statistic.toFixed(2)}</code><br>
A perfect fit would give 0. Now see how large χ² usually gets from noise alone:</div>`
}
```

```{ojs}
viewof alpha = {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)
  const parsed = Number(params.get("alpha"))
  let value = 0.05
  if (parsed >= 0.005 && parsed <= 0.2) value = parsed
  const input = Inputs.range([0.005, 0.2], {step: 0.005, value, label: "α (significance level)"})
  input.classList.add("ojs-fill")
  return input
}
```

```{ojs}
// A plain-language readout of the decision, with the formal notation kept
// as a smaller second line rather than leading with it.
verdict = {
  const r = result
  if (!r.ok) {
    return html`<div class="htest-verdict htest-verdict--none">Enter valid inputs above and click <strong>Run test</strong>.</div>`
  }

  // Turn a p-value into "how often chance alone would do this".
  const chance = p => {
    if (p < 1e-4) return "less than 1 in 10,000 times"
    if (p > 0.99) return "almost always"
    if (p < 0.5) return `about 1 in ${Math.round(1 / p)} times`
    return `about ${Math.round(p * 100)}% of the time`
  }

  const name = testMeta[r.test].full
  const sym = testMeta[r.test].symbol
  let dfText = `${r.df}`
  if (r.test === "F") dfText = `${r.df1}, ${r.df2}`
  const pText = r.pValue < 1e-4 ? "p < 0.0001" : `p = ${r.pValue.toFixed(4)}`

  let plain
  if (r.test === "t") {
    const gap = Math.abs(r.mean1 - r.mean2)
    const dir = r.mean1 >= r.mean2 ? "higher" : "lower"
    plain = r.reject
      ? html`Group 1's mean is <strong>${gap.toPrecision(3)}</strong> ${dir} than Group 2's. If the two groups were really the same, a gap that size would turn up ${chance(r.pValue)} — so this is <strong>more than noise: the difference looks real.</strong>`
      : html`Group 1's mean is <strong>${gap.toPrecision(3)}</strong> ${dir} than Group 2's, but a gap that size would still turn up ${chance(r.pValue)} even if the groups were the same. <strong>Not enough evidence to call it a real difference.</strong>`
  } else if (r.test === "F") {
    const vr = (r.sd1 * r.sd1) / (r.sd2 * r.sd2)
    plain = r.reject
      ? html`Group 1's variance is <strong>${vr.toPrecision(3)}×</strong> Group 2's. A ratio this far from 1 would happen ${chance(r.pValue)} if the spreads were truly equal — so <strong>the spreads really do differ.</strong>`
      : html`Group 1's variance is <strong>${vr.toPrecision(3)}×</strong> Group 2's, but a ratio that far from 1 would happen ${chance(r.pValue)} even with equal spreads. <strong>Not enough evidence that the spreads differ.</strong>`
  } else {
    plain = r.reject
      ? html`The observed counts pull away from the model by <strong>χ² = ${r.statistic.toFixed(2)}</strong>. A mismatch that large would happen ${chance(r.pValue)} if the model were right — so <strong>the data doesn't fit the model.</strong>`
      : html`The observed counts pull away from the model by <strong>χ² = ${r.statistic.toFixed(2)}</strong>, which would happen ${chance(r.pValue)} even if the model were right. <strong>No real evidence against the model.</strong>`
  }

  return html`<div class="htest-verdict ${r.reject ? "htest-verdict--reject" : "htest-verdict--keep"}">
    <div class="htest-verdict-plain">${plain}</div>
    <div class="htest-verdict-formal">${name} · ${sym}(${dfText}) = ${r.statistic.toFixed(3)} · ${pText} · ${r.reject ? "reject H₀" : "fail to reject H₀"} at α = ${alpha}</div>
  </div>`
}
```

```{ojs}
detailsTable = {

  if (!r.ok) return document.createElement("div")

  if (r.test === "t") {

      ["Mean difference x̅1 − x̅2", (r.mean1 - r.mean2).toPrecision(6)],
      ["Pooled variance sₚ²", r.pooledVar.toPrecision(6)],

    ]
    return VM.ui.renderTable({html, headers: ["Quantity", "Value"], rows, csvHeaders: ["Quantity", "Value"], filename: "t-test-details.csv"})
  }

  if (r.test === "F") {
    const critParts = []
    for (const value of r.critLines) critParts.push(value.toPrecision(5))
    const critText = critParts.join(",  ")
    const rows = [
      ["Group 1 variance s₁²", (r.sd1 * r.sd1).toPrecision(6)],
      ["Group 2 variance s₂²", (r.sd2 * r.sd2).toPrecision(6)],
      ["F = s₁² / s₂²", r.statistic.toPrecision(6)],
      ["Degrees of freedom", `${r.df1}, ${r.df2}`],
      ["Critical value(s) at α", critText],
      ["p-value", r.pValue.toExponential(4)],
      ["Decision", r.reject ? "reject H₀" : "fail to reject H₀"]
    ]
    return VM.ui.renderTable({html, headers: ["Quantity", "Value"], rows, csvHeaders: ["Quantity", "Value"], filename: "f-test-details.csv"})
  }

  const rows = []
  for (const cat of r.categories) {
    rows.push([cat.label, cat.o.toString(), cat.e.toPrecision(5), (cat.o - cat.e).toPrecision(4), cat.contrib.toPrecision(5)])
  }
  rows.push(["Σ", r.total.toString(), r.total.toPrecision(5), "0", r.statistic.toPrecision(5)])
  return VM.ui.renderTable({
    html,
    headers: ["Category", "Observed", "Expected", "O − E", "(O − E)² / E"],
    csvHeaders: ["Category", "Observed", "Expected", "O - E", "(O - E)^2 / E"],
    filename: "chi-square-details.csv",
    rows
  })
}
```

::::

## The three tests

All three answer the same shape of question — *is what we observed more extreme than chance alone would usually produce?* — by reducing the data to a single number and asking where that number falls on a known reference distribution. The toggle at the top switches which test (and which distribution) is in view; the two-group summary is shared between the t-test and the F-test, so you can flip between "are the means different?" and "are the spreads different?" on the same data.

### t-test

The two-sample $t$-test compares two group means. With pooled variance $s_p^2$ and standard error $\text{SE} = s_p\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{n_1} + \tfrac{1}{n_2}}$,

$$
t = \frac{\bar x_1 - \bar x_2}{\text{SE}}, \qquad \text{df} = n_1 + n_2 - 2 .
$$

Under $H_0: \mu_1 = \mu_2$ this follows Student's $t$ distribution. The data panel shows the observed mean gap against the **least significant difference** $t^* \cdot \text{SE}$: when the gap bar is longer than the threshold bar, the result is significant. This page uses the pooled (equal-variance) form; with very unequal spreads, Welch's $t$-test is the better choice.

### F-test

The $F$-test compares two variances. With $F = s_1^2 / s_2^2$ and degrees of freedom $(n_1 - 1,\ n_2 - 1)$, this follows the $F$ distribution under $H_0: \sigma_1^2 = \sigma_2^2$. Because $F$ is a ratio, the null value is $1$, not $0$, and the distribution is not symmetric. The data panel shades each group's $\pm 1$ SD band — the ratio of their widths, squared, is $F$. The $F$-test is sensitive to non-normal data, more so than the $t$-test.

### Chi-square test

The $\chi^2$ goodness-of-fit test compares observed category counts $O_i$ to the counts $E_i$ a reference model predicts:

$$
\chi^2 = \sum_{i} \frac{(O_i - E_i)^2}{E_i}, \qquad \text{df} = k - 1 .
$$

Each term is one category's contribution — the bar labels in the data panel — and they sum to the statistic. Large values mean the observed counts stray far from the model, so the test is always one-sided (right tail). It relies on a large-sample approximation; a common rule of thumb is every $E_i \ge 5$.
